industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying a view that moved inside the industry this week: Software B2B Enterprise goes to Neutral on the rotation into software, Semiconductors stays Underweight on the AI capital spending re-pricing, Hardware stays Neutral with the evidence moved against it at the margin. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the market has stopped paying for AI capital spending (hyperscaler prints gave no lift, ABB sold on data-centre orders) while demand is intact and sub-sector upgrades continue (memory, equipment, power electronics), and the software-against-semiconductors factor pair is reversing (Goldman Sachs' desk, 26 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, B prior. The industry row stays C because the industry is split by the rotation itself. Counter-case for D: the Nasdaq down 6% in two weeks with momentum down 15% is a regime statement about this industry; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Underweight, carried, with the tape now agreeing: Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: D now, A prior, the sharpest fall in technology, where last week's reading still ranked the sector B. The two conditions for Neutral (the AI credit channel stabilising; a second house joining Jefferies' European call) could not be tested because no strategist reached the pack; the only artificial-intelligence item is an undated headline that low AI exposure is Europe's edge. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Of the Pool's semiconductor names, Technoprobe, AT&S, INFICON, Sensirion, STMicroelectronics, Soitec, AIXTRON and AMS Osram are marked leaving the Pool or meet a Sell Criterion, so the row's cost to the Lists is falling of its own accord. Counter-case: demand was never the problem and European exposure is equipment, power and optics. To C when the AI credit channel is read stable or a second house joins the European call, with relative strength holding C or better.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park, on price and not on quality; conviction medium (the direction of the multiple is a judgement with wide error bands, the business judgement is firm). The record does not progress the case and does not invalidate it: a hold-ready case. Re-engage at or below about EUR 650 to 700, or when the 24-month-forward multiple is at or below 18.7x, or after a cycle-peak de-rating in the sector with the 1.4 nanometre and DRAM engines intact. The next company test is 27 October 2026, Q3 2026 results against the EUR 1,100 million revenue guide. The gate line does not park the case (no D or F on management B, business quality A, predictability B, trackability C); the return does: the 'Modal return' is about minus 2 percent a year to April 2028 and plus 1 percent a year to October 2029 against the 20 percent bar.
case: - The thesis in one line: a demand inflection in the best business of its cohort, caught after the market has recognised it; the change is real and mostly delivered, the business is as good as the sell-side says, and the price asks us to bet that the market keeps paying a mid-cycle multiple through the cycle's turn; we decline that bet now and would take it about a quarter lower.

- The change is external and the strongest in the set. Gate-all-around transistors raise deposition content per wafer mechanically: about USD 400 million of served market per 100,000 monthly wafer starts at 2 nanometres; USD 450 to 500 million more at 1.4 nanometres, with pilot lines taking tools from the second half of 2026; USD 400 to 450 million at 4F2 DRAM from 2028. Transistor-level layers rise from about 50 percent of ALD layers at 2 nanometres to about 60 at 1.4. The capacity leg is cyclical and visible: TSMC capital spending USD 60 to 64 billion; Tokyo Electron's wafer fab equipment forecast at least USD 150 billion in 2026 and USD 190 billion in 2027; Morgan Stanley USD 163, 223 and 254 billion for 2026 to 2028; Deutsche Bank sees demand visible to the end of 2028.

- The change has travelled the whole 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain: record quarterly revenue of EUR 1,003 million in Q2 2026, adjusted operating margin 33.0 percent against a 28 to 32 percent target range, the 2027 outlook raised above the top of a range set ten months earlier, consensus FY2027 earnings per share up 57 percent in twelve months to EUR 32.62, revision-momentum score 15.
counter_case: - The bull's case at full force: ASM is the single best-placed company in the wafer fab equipment cohort for the two transitions that matter this decade, gate-all-around logic and then 4F2 and 3D DRAM; its content per wafer rises with every node independent of unit growth; it is sole-source where it counts; it has just entered three new markets (metal ALD, DRAM epitaxy, CMP); its estimates are still rising on every window; it is self-funded with EUR 1.1 billion of net cash; the sector's demand read is the strongest in the pack. Consensus is still too low: Morgan Stanley's FY2027 revenue of EUR 5.5 billion was 15 percent above consensus when set and "merely matches consensus market growth"; ING models a 22 percent organic revenue compound rate to 2030 against the company's "at least 12 percent" and calls the guidance conservative; Deutsche Bank says consensus "failed to capture the company's true long-term earnings power"; an expert argues the cycle could run ten years. The multiple has already fallen from 35.9x at the five-year peak to 23.7x, the 35th percentile of five years, a discount to US deposition peers at about 25x and a five-turn discount to the front-end peers on Morgan Stanley's count; ING calls the discount unjustified; Deutsche Bank's EUR 1,100 target is 27x FY2028 earnings; the bull houses' targets of EUR 1,100 to EUR 1,350 are 25 to 53 percent above the price; on consensus earnings and a held multiple the eighteen-month return is about 20 percent a year, a B. The content growth is structural, so the riskiness the record rates D is the memory of a re-rating that is over, and the stock is a structural grower at a cyclical multiple.

- Against 'Foundations': the moat is narrower than the share suggests, because customers qualify second vendors on principle, ASM's platform throughput and software lag the multi-chamber peers on its own former engineers' evidence, Jefferies believes ASM lost DRAM ALD share over two years, and the next battlegrounds (metal ALD, memory) are ones where Lam (ALTUS Halo molybdenum in production) and Applied (Trillium and Centris Spectral under evaluation) start ahead; the first process-tool-of-record loss at a critical layer is the moment the market reprices the franchise.
triggers: - Re-entry: price at or below about EUR 650 to 700; the 24-month-forward multiple at or below 18.7x; a cycle-peak de-rating in the sector with the 1.4 nanometre and DRAM engines intact. About EUR 600 on the drop-through sensitivity.

- The next company test: Q3 2026 results on 27 October 2026 against the EUR 1,100 million guide; then FY2026 results and the first 2027 guidance in early 2027, with the EUR 4.6 billion floor to be lifted and a possible new 2030 target set.

- The multiple's swing condition: whether hyperscaler and TSMC capital-spending guidance for 2028 is still rising at this time next year (the bull branch at 25x, about 40 percent) or the cycle is seen to peak (the de-rating branch at about 18.5x, about 60 percent). The alarm levels: a TSMC capital-spending cut; FY2028 consensus earnings per share cut more than 5 percent in a quarter; the multiple above 27.1x moves the entry further away.

- The earnings path: 1.4 nanometre pilot shipments slipping past mid-2027 or a quarter below the guided range would change our mind on FY2027 revenue of about EUR 5.4 billion; FY2027 revenue guided below EUR 5.0 billion at the FY2026 results invalidates the content-capture driver.
- The gross margin: two quarters below 50 percent would change our mind on normalisation to about 51 percent; below 47 percent, the company's own floor, invalidates.

- The core franchise: a competitor evaluation announced at a critical high-k or epitaxy step is the alarm; a competitor tool of record for a critical ALD or epitaxy layer at TSMC, Intel or Samsung at 1.4 nanometres, or a sequential decline in research engagements and pilot-line deliveries for that node, invalidates.
